name: Black Cumin
description: Black Cumin (Nigella sativa) represents the dried seeds of a flowering Ranunculaceae annual, functioning as a high-density botanical reservoir of bioactive phytochemicals and essential metabolic micronutrients. Its architectural composition features a robust lignocellulosic scaffold enclosing storage proteins and lipophilic volatile oils, specifically dominated by the quinone-based alkaloid thymoquinone. This seed serves as a potent functional food matrix, mediating systemic inflammatory responses, optimizing cellular glucose uptake, and providing deep immunomodulatory support through complex enzymatic interactions in the gastrointestinal and pulmonary pathways.
macroIntro: The macronutrient profile of Nigella sativa comprises a dense, low-moisture energetic pool of structural storage proteins, polyunsaturated fatty acids, and complex insoluble carbohydrates.
microIntro: An exceptionally concentrated assembly of trivalent metabolic cations, essential divalent minerals, and volatile lipophilic bioactive compounds.

macroNutrients.name: Calories
macroNutrients.description: Thermodynamic energy density derived from the comprehensive beta-oxidation of seed lipids and partial enzymatic hydrolysis of storage globulins.

macroNutrients.name: Protein
macroNutrients.description: High-quality storage globulins providing a diverse amino acid profile, including essential precursors for systemic neurotransmitter synthesis.

macroNutrients.name: Total Fat
macroNutrients.description: Lipid fraction dominated by linoleic and oleic acids, essential for maintaining fluidity in biological lipid bilayers and systemic signaling.

macroNutrients.name: Total Carbohydrates
macroNutrients.description: A complex carbohydrate matrix primarily composed of non-starch structural polysaccharides and trace quantities of plant-derived monosaccharides.

microNutrients.name: Dietary Fiber
microNutrients.description: An extreme density of structural cellulose and hemicellulose that optimizes colonic mechanical motility and serves as a prebiotic microbial substrate.

microNutrients.name: Iron
microNutrients.description: An essential transition metal necessary for hemoglobin oxygen transport and cytochrome-based mitochondrial cellular respiration.

microNutrients.name: Calcium
microNutrients.description: A critical divalent cation supporting hydroxyapatite bone mineralization, myofibril contraction, and regulated intracellular signal transduction.

microNutrients.name: Zinc
microNutrients.description: A vital cofactor for over 300 enzymes, including DNA polymerases and zinc-finger transcription factors governing immune cell proliferation.

microNutrients.name: Magnesium
microNutrients.description: An essential intracellular electrolyte required for ATP enzymatic stabilization and the modulation of hyperexcitable neurological pathways.

microNutrients.name: Thymoquinone
microNutrients.description: The primary bioactive monoterpene quinone that exerts potent antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activity by suppressing nuclear factor-kappa B pathways.

healthBenefits: Immune Architecture Optimization: Thymoquinone directly upregulates the functional capacity of natural killer cells and macrophages, creating a systemic enhancement of the innate host defense response.
Bronchial Smooth Muscle Relaxation: Volatile seed components inhibit histamine release and suppress pro-inflammatory leukotrienes, acting as effective spasmolytics for the pulmonary bronchial tree.

Metabolic Homeostasis and Glucose Sensitivity: Nigella sativa facilitates increased insulin receptor expression and inhibits hepatic gluconeogenesis, significantly improving fasting glycemic control and lipid clearance.

Gastrointestinal Mucosal Shielding: The lipid fraction and active phytoconstituents create an anti-secretory effect in the stomach, directly inhibiting the growth of H. pylori and reducing lipid peroxidation in the gastric mucosa.
precautionsIntro: Given the potent bioactivity of thymoquinone and the seed's metabolic impact, medicinal use requires strict clinical consideration:
precautions: Uterine Smooth Muscle Modulation: Pharmacological doses can induce non-specific contractions, posing an unacceptable risk of instability during gestational stages.

Hemostatic Cascade Interference: Natural inhibitors within the oil fraction may exert an anti-platelet effect, necessitating cessation of therapy prior to invasive surgical procedures to prevent excessive hemorrhage.
Synergistic Hypoglycemic Potentiation: Concurrent consumption with insulin or oral antidiabetic agents can lead to sudden, unbuffered glucose drops, requiring vigilant glycaemic monitoring.
